passages.title: The Umbrella Tag at the Entrance
passages.body: It rained before school on Tuesday. At the entrance, Mina saw two black umbrellas in the same stand. She needed her class umbrella for an outdoor lesson. One umbrella had a small blue tag, but the other had no tag. Mina checked the lending list near the door. The list said, ‘Class 1-2: black umbrella, blue tag.’ She also saw 1-2 on the back of the tag. Mina took that umbrella and left the other one there. She used the list and the tag, so she did not take another class's umbrella.
passages.fullTranslation: 火曜日、登校前に雨が降りました。玄関でミナは、同じ傘立てに黒い傘が二本あるのを見つけました。ミナは、屋外授業で自分のクラスが使う傘を必要としていました。一方の傘には小さな青い札がありましたが、もう一方には札がありませんでした。ミナはドアの近くの貸出表を確認しました。表には「1年2組：黒い傘、青い札」と書かれていました。札の裏にも1-2と書かれていました。ミナはその傘を取り、もう一本はそこに残しました。表と札の両方を確かめたので、別のクラスの傘を持っていかずにすみました。

passages.title: A Note under the Music Stand
passages.body: After music class, Ren found a small note under a music stand. It said, ‘Practice in Room 3 at four.’ There were two school bands, so Ren did not know the right group for the note. He looked at the room schedule on the wall. The brass band used Room 3 at four, and the guitar club used it at five. Ren carried the note to the brass band teacher. The teacher thanked him and put the note on the band's board. Ren did not guess from the room alone. He checked the time too, and that helped him choose the right group.
passages.fullTranslation: 音楽の授業の後、レンは譜面台の下に小さなメモを見つけました。そこには「4時に第3室で練習」と書かれていました。学校には二つの音楽グループがあったので、レンにはどちらのグループのメモか分かりませんでした。壁の部屋予定表を見ると、吹奏楽部は4時に第3室を使い、ギター部は5時に使うことが分かりました。レンはメモを吹奏楽部の先生に届けました。先生は礼を言い、メモを部の掲示板に貼りました。レンは部屋だけで決めつけず、時間も確認したので、正しいグループを選べました。

passages.title: The Two Lunch Bags
passages.body: At lunch, Saki saw two green bags on a table. One was hers, but both bags looked almost the same. She first looked for her name, but the labels only showed the letters S.K. and S.M. Then Saki remembered the food card in her bag. Her card had a red circle. She did not eat one kind of nut. She carefully opened only the small outside pocket of the S.K. bag and saw the red card. She knew the bag was hers. She left the S.M. bag closed and said, “Your bag is here,” to her friend.

passages.title: The Wet Footprints by the Window
passages.body: During the lunch break, Kota went to the library and saw wet footprints near a window. A student was standing there with a book, so Kota first thought the student brought water inside. He did not say anything. He looked around and found a yellow cleaning sign behind a shelf. Then he saw a cloth and a small bucket near the window. The librarian came back. She said rain came through the open window that morning. She cleaned most of the floor, but the corner was still wet. The student was only waiting for the floor to dry. Kota was glad. He checked the area first and did not blame anyone. He helped move one chair away from the wet place. Before leaving, Kota noticed that the footprints stopped beside the cloth, not at the student’s shoes. That was one more reason to wait for an explanation.

passages.title: Which Ball Is for Our Team?
passages.body: Aya's volleyball team had practice after school. In the gym, she found two new volleyballs beside the wall. They were the same color and size. Aya did not want to use another team's ball. She checked the small number on each ball. One said 14 and the other said 18. Then she looked at the practice chart. Her team had Ball 18 on Tuesday, and another team had Ball 14. Aya took Ball 18 to her team. Later, the other team came and found Ball 14 in the same place. The number and the chart made the choice clear.
passages.fullTranslation: アヤのバレーボールチームは放課後に練習がありました。体育館で、壁のそばに新しいバレーボールが二つありました。色も大きさも同じでした。アヤは別のチームのボールを使いたくありませんでした。それぞれのボールの小さな番号を見ると、一つは14、もう一つは18でした。次に練習表を見ると、火曜日は自分のチームが18番、別のチームが14番を使うことになっていました。アヤは18番を自分のチームへ持っていきました。後で別のチームが来ると、14番は同じ場所に残っていました。番号と表を確認したので、正しく選べました。

passages.title: The Missing Plant Marker
passages.body: Haru's class grew three kinds of plants by the classroom window. On Friday, one name marker fell out of a pot. Haru found the marker on the floor, but the right pot was not clear. He looked at the planting map in the class notebook. The middle pot had the word ‘basil.’ Then he compared the leaves with a picture from Monday. The middle plant had the same round leaves as the basil in the picture. Haru put the marker into that pot. He showed the map and the picture to his teacher. The teacher said, “Good check.”
passages.fullTranslation: ハルのクラスは教室の窓辺で三種類の植物を育てていました。金曜日、一つの鉢から名前の札が抜け落ちました。ハルは床で札を見つけましたが、どの鉢に戻すべきかはっきりしませんでした。クラスのノートにある植え付け図を見ると、真ん中の鉢には「バジル」という言葉がありました。さらに月曜日の写真と葉を比べると、真ん中の植物には写真のバジルと同じ丸い葉がありました。ハルはその鉢に札を戻しました。図と写真を先生に見せました。先生は「よく確かめたね」と言いました。

passages.title: The Quiet Bell after Lunch
passages.body: Nao heard a small bell in the hallway just after lunch. It was not the usual school bell, and no one in her class moved. She wondered where the sound came from. At 1:05, she heard it again near the library. Nao looked at a notice beside the library door. It said, “Reading Week book return: 1:00-1:15.” It also said, “Ring the small desk bell when the return box is full.” Nao then saw two students carrying books to the desk. She understood that the sound was not an emergency signal. She returned her own book and helped the librarian place an empty box beside the desk. The time, the notice, and the students' actions all explained the bell. The empty box arrived, and the bell stopped. This matched the notice exactly.
passages.fullTranslation: ナオは昼食のすぐ後、廊下で小さなベルの音を聞きました。いつもの学校のベルではなく、クラスの誰も動きませんでした。ナオはどこから聞こえたのだろうと思いました。1時5分、図書室の近くでまた音がしました。図書室のドアの横の掲示には「読書週間の本の返却：1時〜1時15分」とありました。さらに「返却箱がいっぱいになったら小さな卓上ベルを鳴らしてください」と書かれていました。ナオは本を机へ運ぶ二人の生徒も見ました。それで、その音が緊急の合図ではないと分かりました。自分の本を返し、司書が空の箱を机のそばに置くのを手伝いました。時間、掲示、生徒たちの行動がすべてベルの理由を示していました。 空の箱が届くとベルは止まりました。この様子も掲示の説明とぴったり合っていました。

passages.title: A Different Page Number
passages.body: The teacher said to Riku, “Please give out these English worksheets.” He found two piles on the teacher's desk. The first pile started on page 32, but the second started on page 34. Both had the same lesson title. Riku almost mixed the piles together. Then he looked at the board. On the board, he saw, ‘Today: pages 32-33. Next class: pages 34-35.’ Riku gave his classmates the first pile and left the second pile on the desk. The teacher came in and said, “Thank you for checking.” A small page number stopped a simple mistake.

passages.title: Why the Clock Was Ten Minutes Fast
passages.body: Toma came to school for a Saturday activity. The classroom clock showed 8:40, but his phone showed 8:30. He thought the clock was broken. Before changing it, he checked the clock in the hall. It also showed 8:40. Then Toma read a note on the activity board. It said, ‘For today's event, the clocks in Rooms 2 and 3 are ten minutes ahead. Please be ready before each group arrives.’ The first visitors were coming at 9:00. Toma understood the reason. The clocks were ten minutes fast on purpose. The student staff got ready early. He left the clock alone. At 8:50 on his phone, the room clock showed 9:00, and the student staff were already ready at the door. The note also said, “Check your own phones for the real time before you open the doors.” That detail showed that the faster clocks were only a preparation tool, not the official event time.

passages.title: The Empty Seat on the Bus List
passages.body: Yuna checked the bus list before a class trip. Every student's name was on the list, but Seat 12 was empty. She worried. Maybe one student had no seat. Then she saw a small note beside Seat 12: ‘Camera box.’ The class had a large box for two school cameras, and the teacher did not want it in the aisle. Yuna counted the names again. All thirty students had seats, and Seat 12 was the only place without a name. She said to her friend, “No student is missing.” The empty seat had a job of its own.

passages.title: A Box with Two Arrows
passages.body: Shun carried old paper to the recycling corner. One box had two arrows on its side. A blue arrow pointed to a narrow opening, and a gray arrow pointed to a larger opening. Shun first thought both openings were for paper. He read the words under the arrows. The blue side said ‘flat paper,’ and the gray side said ‘paper cups.’ His papers were flat worksheets, so he used the blue opening. Later, a teacher said, “Paper cups need a different process.” Shun was glad. He read the words and did not use the larger opening only for its size.

passages.title: The Picture without a Name
passages.body: Emi helped prepare a classroom art display. One picture had no name card, and its artist was not clear. Emi did not want to write a name without evidence. She noticed a tiny star in the lower right corner. In an older class folder, she found three pictures with the same star. All three belonged to Ken. She also checked the date on the back of the new picture. It matched Ken's group week for that theme. Emi showed the picture to Ken before she made a new card. Ken smiled and said it was his. He forgot to write his name because the bell rang at the end of class. Emi added the card only after the symbol, the date, and Ken's answer agreed. The teacher then wrote Ken’s name in the class record too. Now the picture and the record had the same name.

passages.title: The Key near the Shoe Box
passages.body: Daichi found a key near the shoe boxes after school. The key had a yellow tag with the number 4. He did not try it in nearby doors. He did not know the right door for the key. Instead, he took it to the staff room. A teacher checked the school key list. Number 4 was the spare key for the art room. The art teacher was still in the building and confirmed that one spare key was missing. Daichi gave the key to the teacher. He was glad. He checked the tag and the list, and he did not test the key himself.

passages.title: A Blue Line on the Floor
passages.body: Mio saw a blue line of tape on the school floor before an open-school event. It started at the front door but did not go toward the usual office. She thought, “Is this line here by mistake?” At the next corner, she found a sign: ‘Visitors: follow the blue line. The main hall is under repair.’ Mio followed the line and reached a side entrance to the meeting room. Later, two visitors said, “Where do we go?” Mio showed them the blue line and the sign. The line looked strange at first, but it was a temporary guide. It went around the repair area.

passages.title: The Book Returned Too Early
passages.body: Kenta was helping with a small book display in the library. On Wednesday, he saw one display book on the normal shelf. He thought, “Is the display over?” and started to move the other books too. Then he checked the card beside the display. It said the display would continue until Friday. Kenta also looked at the return slip inside the missing book. A student borrowed it before the display began and returned it that morning. Kenta showed the slip to the librarian before he moved the book. She checked the date and said, “The student made a mistake.” The student did not know that the book now belonged on the special table. Kenta told the librarian, and they put the book back on the display. He left the other books where they were. Checking both the event card and the return slip showed him why one book had moved early.

passages.title: The Small Star on the Map
passages.body: Rina met a visitor near the school entrance. The visitor wanted to find the nurse's room. Rina opened a school map, but two rooms near the center had similar shapes. One had a small star beside it. Rina checked the map legend. The star meant ‘health and first aid.’ The other room had a square mark for the office. Rina followed the path from the entrance to the star and walked with the visitor. They reached the nurse's room without going into the office first. The small symbol and the legend made the map clear.

passages.title: The Library Seat Survey
passages.body: The library committee wanted to make quiet study easier. For one week, Mei and Koki counted how many seats were used before school and after school. In the morning, most students sat near the windows because the light was good. After school, those seats were often noisy because club members met near the entrance. The committee had planned to put all the ‘Quiet Study’ signs by the windows. However, the survey showed a different need. They moved two signs to the back tables for after-school users and left one sign near the windows for the morning. A second count three days later showed that more students chose the quiet area. The committee learned that the best place for a sign can change with time.
passages.fullTranslation: 図書委員会は、静かに勉強しやすい場所を作りたいと考えました。1週間、メイとコウキは登校前と放課後に、どの席がどれくらい使われているかを数えました。朝は、光がよく入るので多くの生徒が窓の近くに座っていました。放課後は、入口の近くで部活動の生徒が集まるため、その席はよくにぎやかになりました。委員会は当初、「静かに学習」の表示をすべて窓側に置く予定でした。しかし調査から別の必要が分かりました。放課後の利用者のために表示を二つ奥の机へ移し、朝のために一つだけ窓側に残しました。3日後にもう一度数えると、静かな場所を選ぶ生徒が増えていました。委員会は、表示に最適な場所は時間によって変わることを学びました。

passages.title: A Message That Arrived Twice
passages.body: On Monday, the class received the same festival message twice. One copy came from the student council list, and another came from the class event list. Some students thought the second message included new information, so they read both carefully. Aya compared the two messages and found that every detail was the same. She asked the teachers managing the lists. They learned that both lists included all second-year students. Before the next event, the class chose one list for general notices and kept the other only for messages about class jobs. They also added a short line saying where each message came from. The next notice arrived only once, and students could understand its purpose immediately. A small change made communication clearer.
passages.fullTranslation: 月曜日、クラスに同じ文化祭のお知らせが二度届きました。一通は生徒会の配信リストから、もう一通はクラス行事のリストからでした。二通目には新しい情報があると思った生徒もいたので、両方を注意して読みました。アヤが二つを比べると、内容はすべて同じでした。そこで、リストを管理している先生たちに尋ねました。調べると、どちらのリストにも2年生全員が入っていることが分かりました。次の行事の前に、一般のお知らせには一つのリストだけを使い、もう一つはクラスの係の連絡専用にしました。また、各メッセージがどこから来たかを示す短い一文も加えました。次のお知らせは一度だけ届き、生徒たちは目的をすぐ理解できました。小さな変更で連絡が分かりやすくなりました。

passages.title: Testing the New Water Station
passages.body: A new water station was placed outside the gym. During the first week, students often formed a long line after practice. Some people said the machine was too slow and should be replaced. The health committee decided to check before making that request. They measured how long it took to fill ten bottles. The machine itself worked at almost the same speed each time. Then they watched the line. A small table for bags stood directly beside the station, so students had to turn and wait for one another before they could leave. The committee moved the table two meters away and marked a separate place for waiting. The next afternoon, the station served the same number of students, but the line moved much faster. The school did not need a new machine. Careful observation showed that the space around it, not the machine, caused most of the delay. Before moving anything, they also asked two students to describe where the line felt slow. Both pointed to the narrow space beside the table, not to the water flow. This matched the timing results and gave the committee another reason to test the layout first.

passages.title: The Sign Nobody Saw
passages.body: The art club made a poster for its open room. They placed it low on a wall near the stairs because the colors looked bright there. During lunch, however, few students entered. Yuto stood in the crowded hallway to see why. Bags and students blocked the lower wall, and he could not read the club name from several meters away. The members tested the same poster in two higher places. They asked ten students to walk from the stairs and say when they noticed it. More students saw it early when it was at eye level near the corner. The club moved the poster there instead of printing a larger one. The next day, more visitors found the room.

passages.title: Two Ways to Borrow a Tablet
passages.body: The school library offered two ways to borrow a tablet. One card showed four written steps. Another had a QR code that opened a guide. Either method worked well for older students, but many first-time users asked the same questions. Nana watched them and noticed a problem. The written card used ‘device number’ before showing where that number was. The online guide showed the number first but hid the return rule on its last page. The committee combined the useful parts. A new card used one photo, three short steps, and one clear return rule. A QR code remained for anyone wanting more detail. After the change, fewer users needed help, while both borrowing methods stayed available.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校の図書室には、タブレットを借りる方法が二つありました。一つのカードには四つの手順が文章で書かれ、もう一つには案内を開くQRコードがありました。上級生にはどちらの方法も使いやすいものでしたが、初めての利用者の多くは同じ質問をしていました。ナナが様子を見ると問題に気付きました。文章のカードは「端末番号」という言葉を、その番号の場所を示す前に使っていました。一方、オンライン案内は番号を最初に示していましたが、返却の決まりが最後のページにありました。委員会は良い部分を組み合わせました。新しいカードでは写真一枚、三つの短い手順、一つの明確な返却ルールを使いました。詳しく知りたい人のためにQRコードも残しました。変更後、助けを求める利用者が減り、二つの借り方も残せました。

passages.title: The Ramp Route after Rain
passages.body: The student council was preparing a guide for visitors who used wheelchairs. Two routes led from the school gate to the hall. Route A was thirty meters shorter, so the first draft called it the better route. Before printing the guide, Miki suggested walking both routes after rain. The next wet morning, the team checked them with a teacher. Route A crossed a smooth stone area near the garden. Water stayed there, and one part was slippery. Route B was longer, but it had a covered path and a gentle ramp with a rough surface. The team also timed both routes. Route B took only two minutes longer. They changed the guide to recommend Route B on rainy days and added a note about Route A for dry weather. The shortest route was not always the safest or most useful one. The team wrote both results in the guide instead of calling one route good and the other bad. That way, visitors could understand why the rainy-day recommendation was different and could choose with the weather in mind.

passages.title: Why the Lost-and-Found Box Stayed Full
passages.body: The lost-and-found box near the office stayed full for weeks. Every Friday, the student council posted a list, but few owners came. Ryo interviewed six students about things they had lost. They said the list was hard to use. It included words such as ‘small bag’ or ‘blue object,’ but several things matched them. The council changed the recording card. Staff now wrote where an item was found, one special feature, and the date. For example, ‘blue pencil case with a white star, found by the gym on May 12’ was clear. The next two lists used the new details. More items were returned, and the box finally had space. Better information worked better than reminders alone.
passages.fullTranslation: 職員室近くの落とし物箱は、何週間もいっぱいのままでした。毎週金曜日、生徒会は一覧を出していましたが、持ち主はほとんど来ませんでした。リョウが6人の生徒に、なくした物について話を聞くと、一覧が使いにくいと言われました。「小さい袋」「青い物」などの表現では、当てはまる物がいくつもあったのです。生徒会は記録カードを変えました。拾った場所、特徴を一つ、日付を書くようにしました。たとえば「白い星の付いた青い筆箱、5月12日に体育館前で発見」とすれば分かりやすくなります。次の2回の一覧には新しい情報を使いました。返却される物が増え、箱にはようやく空きができました。注意を繰り返すだけより、情報を良くする方が効果的でした。

passages.title: The Club Video without Captions
passages.body: The media club made a two-minute video to introduce school activities. During editing, the members checked the music and pictures many times. Before publishing it, they showed it to students in the cafeteria at lunch. The room was noisy, and several students missed important names in the narration. One student said that key words on the screen would also help when a speaker talked quickly. The club did not record the video again. It added short captions for club names, meeting days, and important instructions. The members tested the new version in the same cafeteria. This time, more students answered three simple questions correctly. The test showed a problem that was invisible in the quiet editing room.

passages.title: A Shorter Line, a Longer Wait
passages.body: At the school festival, two food stands sold different snacks. Visitors kept choosing Stand B because its line looked shorter. However, some of them later said they had waited longer there. The festival team wanted to know why. They counted people in each line every five minutes and also measured the time from ordering to receiving food. Stand A usually had twelve people waiting, but each order took about forty seconds. Stand B often had only seven people, yet each order took nearly ninety seconds because one snack had to be heated after the order. The team put a small sign at both stands showing the usual preparation time. They also prepared part of Stand B's snack before the busiest period. Visitors could then choose with better information, and the longest waits became shorter. Line length alone had hidden the real cause. The team checked again during the final hour to see whether the change only worked once. Stand B still had fewer people in line than Stand A, but its waiting time was now close to the time shown on the sign. The second check supported their explanation.

passages.title: The Map That Faced the Wrong Way
passages.body: Visitors often stopped at the campus map near the front gate and then walked in the wrong direction. The map was correct, so volunteers first planned to add arrows. Sora watched five visitors use it. The top of the map showed north, but people at the gate were facing south. Some turned left on the paper and then turned left with their bodies, although those directions were different. The team printed a test copy rotated to match the view from the gate. They asked five more visitors to find the science room. Four chose the correct path without help. The team kept a small north mark but used the visitor's view as the main direction. Rotating the map worked better than adding many arrows.

passages.title: Three Minutes of Silence
passages.body: Group work in Class 2-1 often began slowly. Students spent several minutes moving chairs, finding papers, and asking what to do. The teacher suggested a three-minute quiet setup before discussion. Some students thought silence would waste time, so the class tested it for four lessons. During those three minutes, everyone read the task, prepared materials, and wrote one idea alone. The class recorded when each group began real discussion. Before the test, most groups needed about six minutes to start. With the quiet setup, they usually started in four minutes, including the silent time. Students also entered the discussion with an idea ready. The setup gave everyone a clear first step, so the class kept it.

passages.title: The Donation Box Question
passages.body: A school charity group placed a donation box near the entrance with a sign that said, ‘School supplies welcome.’ After a week, the box contained many things the group could not use, including broken pens, opened paint, and very large notebooks. The students did not want to blame the donors. They checked the rejected items and asked three families what they thought ‘school supplies’ meant. The answers were different. The group replaced the broad phrase with four clear examples: unopened pencils, clean erasers, A4 notebooks, and rulers under thirty centimeters. It also added two small pictures showing unacceptable items. During the next collection week, the total number of donations was a little lower, but almost every item could be used. Clear examples made the rule easier to understand and reduced waste for the volunteers who sorted the box. The group kept the old sign in its meeting notes so members could compare the two versions later. They also decided to review the accepted-item examples before the next season, because the needs of the receiving group could change.

passages.title: The Door That Looked Closed
passages.body: A meeting room at the community center had a glass door. During an open event, several visitors looked through it and walked away even though the room was open. A sign said, ‘Please close this door after entering.’ From a distance, people noticed only the large word ‘close.’ Student volunteers tested a clearer sign: ‘OPEN — Please enter. Close the door behind you.’ They placed ‘OPEN’ at eye level and moved the smaller instruction below it. During the next hour, the door remained closed as required, but visitors entered without asking whether the room was available. The problem was not the glass door or the rule. The order and size of the words had given the wrong first message.

passages.title: A Practice Schedule with No Break
passages.body: The basketball team planned a ninety-minute practice before an important game. The schedule had three drills with no break because the captain wanted to use every minute. After two practices, the coach asked players to rate each drill. The first drill received strong scores, but mistakes increased later. Several players said they needed a moment to drink water and check the next goal. The team tested a five-minute break after forty minutes. It kept the total practice time the same by shortening repeated instructions. In the next two practices, later drills had fewer simple mistakes. The captain learned that using every minute for movement did not always mean using the whole practice well for everyone.

passages.title: The Refill Cup Experiment
passages.body: For the autumn school event, the environment club wanted to reduce disposable cups. One idea was to use only refill cups that visitors returned after drinking. Before changing the whole system, the club tested two drink stations for one afternoon. Station A used disposable cups. Station B gave visitors a strong cup with a return token. The students counted cups, return rates, waiting time, and the minutes needed for washing. Most refill cups came back, but the washing table became crowded just before the final performance. Disposable cups were faster but created much more trash. The club chose a mixed plan for the real event. Refill cups were used during normal hours, while one small supply of disposable cups was kept for the busiest twenty minutes and for visitors who needed them. The experiment helped the club reduce waste without creating a new service problem. After the event, the club compared its records with the previous year. Trash from drink cups had fallen, and the waiting time stayed within the limit the organizers had set. The members wrote both benefits and problems in their report so the next team could improve the plan again.
passages.fullTranslation: 秋の学校行事に向けて、環境部は使い捨てカップを減らしたいと考えました。すべて返却式のカップにする案がありましたが、全体を変える前に、午後の間だけ二つの飲み物コーナーで試しました。Aでは使い捨てカップを使い、Bでは丈夫なカップと返却用の印を渡しました。生徒たちは、使用数、返却率、待ち時間、洗うのに必要な時間を記録しました。返却式カップの多くは戻ってきましたが、最後の発表の直前には洗い場が混雑しました。使い捨ては速い一方、ごみがずっと多く出ました。そこで本番では混合方式にしました。通常の時間は返却式を使い、最も混む20分間と必要な来場者のために、少量の使い捨ても用意しました。実験によって、新しいサービス上の問題を作らずにごみを減らせました。 行事の後、部員は記録を前年と比べました。飲み物用カップのごみは減り、待ち時間も主催者が決めた範囲に収まりました。次の担当者がさらに改善できるよう、報告書には良かった点と問題点の両方を書きました。

passages.title: Who Could Hear the Announcement?
passages.body: Teachers received reports that some students could not hear the afternoon announcement. It sounded clear in the office, so the cause was not obvious. A student team tested the message in the library, at the east stairs, and in the old music hall. They wrote down which words they missed. The first two places were fine. In the music hall, the message became very quiet whenever the fire door in the connecting hallway was closed. The speaker was on the other side. The school did not leave the fire door open. It added a speaker inside the hall and repeated the test with the door closed. All three listeners then heard the complete message. The solution kept the safety rule and fixed the problem.

passages.title: The First Question on the Form
passages.body: The student council made a survey about the school festival. Its first question asked students to choose among five detailed plans for next year. When six first-year students tested the form, three stopped at that question. They said they did not know enough about the plans. The survey team discussed the result and kept the useful question but moved it later. The new first question was simple: ‘Which part of this year's festival did you use or visit?’ Later questions gave short information before asking about future choices. In a second test, all six students reached the end. Changing the order did not remove important thinking. It gave students information and confidence before the hardest question.

passages.title: The Community Freezer Log
passages.body: A community center kept a freezer for donated food. Part of the food was for families who needed help that week, and part was emergency stock for storms. In August, volunteers noticed that several meals had passed their best-use dates while other shelves became almost empty. A group of students studied the freezer log instead of simply asking for more donations. The log recorded the date, food type, number of packs, and whether each pack was marked ‘weekly’ or ‘emergency.’ The students found two patterns. First, new weekly donations were often placed in front of older ones, so volunteers took the newest packs first. Second, emergency stock was checked only once a month, so volunteers sometimes missed items that were close to their dates. The students suggested three changes. Older weekly packs would be placed in a clearly marked front basket. Emergency food would still be protected, but volunteers would check its dates every week and replace near-date packs with newer ones. Finally, the center would write the number of available weekly packs on a small board before accepting extra donations of the same kind. After six weeks, the freezer still held the required emergency amount, but fewer meals were thrown away. The students did not reduce the safety stock. They used the same records more carefully to balance immediate needs and future emergencies. The center kept the old procedure in the file too, so future volunteers could compare the results and understand why the new system had been adopted.

passages.title: A Translation with One Missing Warning
passages.body: The science museum asked a student team to check a new bilingual safety notice. The English notice said visitors could touch the model only when a staff member was present. The Japanese version, however, simply said that visitors could touch the model. Yui first wondered whether the shorter translation was intentional. She compared it with an older notice and then asked the museum educator. The educator explained that the condition was important because one part of the model became hot during demonstrations. The team rewrote the Japanese sentence so that the condition about staff presence was clear. They also checked the other five rules line by line, rather than assuming that the rest were correct because they looked similar. No other meaning was missing. Before the notice was printed, another student read only the Japanese version and correctly explained when touching was allowed. The team learned that a translation can contain almost all the right words and still change a safety rule if one condition disappears.
passages.fullTranslation: 科学博物館は、新しい二言語の安全案内を確認するよう生徒チームに依頼しました。英語の案内には、職員がいるときに限って来館者が模型に触れられると書かれていました。しかし日本語版には、来館者が模型に触れられるとだけ書かれていました。ユイは最初、短い訳が意図的なものかもしれないと考えました。以前の案内と比べ、博物館の担当者にも尋ねました。担当者は、実演中に模型の一部が熱くなるため、その条件は重要だと説明しました。チームは、職員がいるという条件が明確になるよう日本語の文を書き直しました。また、残りも似ているから正しいと決めつけず、ほかの五つの規則を一行ずつ確認しました。ほかに意味の抜けはありませんでした。印刷前に別の生徒が日本語版だけを読み、いつ触れてよいかを正しく説明できました。チームは、ほとんどの言葉が正しくても、一つの条件が消えるだけで安全上の規則の意味が変わることを学びました。

passages.title: The River Path Detour Board
passages.material: route map + closure table + bus schedule
passages.body:
The city planned a weekend river festival, and a junior-high volunteer team was asked to prepare a route guide for visitors arriving at Midori Station. Usually, the shortest walk from the station to the festival field followed the east river path. However, part of that path would be closed for bridge repairs on Saturday morning. The first draft of the guide simply told everyone to use the west path instead. Rina thought that advice was safe but not complete because visitors would arrive at different times and some would come by bus.

The team gathered three pieces of information. The route map showed that the normal east path was 1.2 kilometers, the west walking route was 1.7 kilometers, and a third route used a bus from the station to Library Stop followed by a 0.5-kilometer walk. The construction table said the east path between Bridge A and Gate 2 would be closed from 8:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. After 11:30, the path would reopen, but bicycles would still be prohibited until 2:00 p.m. The bus schedule showed departures from Midori Station at 8:40, 9:10, 9:40, 10:40, and 11:40. The ride to Library Stop took eight minutes.

The team tested three example visitors. A family arriving at 9:00 with a small child could take the 9:10 bus and avoid the longer west walk. A walking club arriving at 10:15 could use the west route immediately instead of waiting twenty-five minutes for the next bus. A visitor arriving at noon could use the reopened east path, which was again the shortest walking route. These examples showed why one fixed instruction would not help everyone.

The final board began with a clear warning about the 8:30–11:30 closure. Under it, the team added a simple choice: before 11:30, use the west walk or check the next bus; after 11:30, walkers may use the east path again. A bicycle symbol remained crossed out until 2:00. The board did not claim that one route was always best. It connected the map, the time of arrival, and the transport schedule so visitors could make a safe choice for their own situation.
passages.fullTranslation:
市では週末に川沿いの祭りを開く予定で、中学生のボランティアチームが、みどり駅に到着する来場者向けの道案内を作ることになりました。通常、駅から会場まで最も短い徒歩ルートは川の東側の道です。しかし土曜日の朝は、橋の工事のためその一部が通行止めになります。最初の案では、全員に西側の道を使うよう案内していました。リナは、それは安全ではあるものの、来場時刻も違い、バスを使う人もいるため十分ではないと考えました。

チームは三つの資料を集めました。地図によると、通常の東側ルートは1.2キロ、西側の徒歩ルートは1.7キロ、三つ目は駅から図書館前までバスに乗り、そこから0.5キロ歩くルートです。工事表には、A橋から第2ゲートまでの東側の道が午前8時30分から11時30分まで閉鎖されるとありました。11時30分以降は再開しますが、自転車は午後2時まで通れません。バス時刻表には、みどり駅発が8時40分、9時10分、9時40分、10時40分、11時40分とあり、図書館前まで8分かかります。

チームは三つの来場例を考えました。9時に小さな子どもと到着する家族は9時10分のバスに乗れば、西側を長く歩かずにすみます。10時15分に到着する徒歩グループなら、次のバスを25分待つより、すぐ西側ルートを歩けます。正午に到着する人は、再開した東側ルートを使え、それが再び最短の徒歩ルートになります。この例から、一つの固定した指示では全員の役に立たないことが分かりました。

完成した案内板では、最初に8時30分から11時30分までの閉鎖をはっきり示しました。その下に、「11時30分までは西側を歩くか次のバスを確認する。11時30分以降は歩行者は東側も利用できる」という簡単な選択を示しました。自転車の印は午後2時まで禁止表示のままです。案内板は、どれか一つの道がいつでも最善だとは言いません。地図、到着時刻、交通時刻表を結び付け、それぞれの状況に合った安全な選択ができるようにしました。

slashRows.english: The city planned a weekend river festival, and a junior-high volunteer team was asked to prepare a route guide for visitors arriving at Midori Station.
slashRows.japanese: 市では週末に川沿いの祭りを開く予定で、中学生のボランティアチームが、みどり駅に到着する来場者向けの道案内を作ることになりました。

slashRows.english: Usually, the shortest walk from the station to the festival field followed the east river path.
slashRows.japanese: 通常、駅から会場まで最も短い徒歩ルートは川の東側の道です。

slashRows.english: However, part of that path would be closed for bridge repairs on Saturday morning.
slashRows.japanese: しかし土曜日の朝は、橋の工事のためその一部が通行止めになります。

slashRows.english: The first draft of the guide simply told everyone to use the west path instead.
slashRows.japanese: 最初の案では、全員に西側の道を使うよう案内していました。

slashRows.english: Rina thought that advice was safe but not complete because visitors would arrive at different times and some would come by bus.
slashRows.japanese: リナは、それは安全ではあるものの、来場時刻も違い、バスを使う人もいるため十分ではないと考えました。

slashRows.english: The team gathered three pieces of information.
slashRows.japanese: チームは三つの資料を集めました。

slashRows.english: The route map showed that the normal east path was 1.2 kilometers, the west walking route was 1.7 kilometers, and a third route used a bus from the station to Library Stop followed by a 0.5-kilometer walk.
slashRows.japanese: 地図によると、通常の東側ルートは1.2キロ、西側の徒歩ルートは1.7キロ、三つ目は駅から図書館前までバスに乗り、そこから0.5キロ歩くルートです。

slashRows.english: The construction table said the east path between Bridge A and Gate 2 would be closed from 8:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m.
slashRows.japanese: 工事表には、A橋から第2ゲートまでの東側の道が午前8時30分から11時30分まで閉鎖されるとありました。

slashRows.english: After 11:30, the path would reopen, but bicycles would still be prohibited until 2:00 p.m.
slashRows.japanese: 11時30分以降は再開しますが、自転車は午後2時まで通れません。

slashRows.english: The bus schedule showed departures from Midori Station at 8:40, 9:10, 9:40, 10:40, and 11:40.
slashRows.japanese: バス時刻表には、みどり駅発が8時40分、9時10分、9時40分、10時40分、11時40分とあり、図書館前まで8分かかります。

slashRows.english: The ride to Library Stop took eight minutes.
slashRows.japanese: チームは三つの来場例を考えました。

slashRows.english: The team tested three example visitors.
slashRows.japanese: 9時に小さな子どもと到着する家族は9時10分のバスに乗れば、西側を長く歩かずにすみます。

slashRows.english: A family arriving at 9:00 with a small child could take the 9:10 bus and avoid the longer west walk.
slashRows.japanese: 10時15分に到着する徒歩グループなら、次のバスを25分待つより、すぐ西側ルートを歩けます。

slashRows.english: A walking club arriving at 10:15 could use the west route immediately instead of waiting twenty-five minutes for the next bus.
slashRows.japanese: 正午に到着する人は、再開した東側ルートを使え、それが再び最短の徒歩ルートになります。

slashRows.english: A visitor arriving at noon could use the reopened east path, which was again the shortest walking route.
slashRows.japanese: この例から、一つの固定した指示では全員の役に立たないことが分かりました。

slashRows.english: These examples showed why one fixed instruction would not help everyone.
slashRows.japanese: 完成した案内板では、最初に8時30分から11時30分までの閉鎖をはっきり示しました。

slashRows.english: The final board began with a clear warning about the 8:30–11:30 closure.
slashRows.japanese: その下に、「11時30分までは西側を歩くか次のバスを確認する。

slashRows.english: Under it, the team added a simple choice: before 11:30, use the west walk or check the next bus; after 11:30, walkers may use the east path again.
slashRows.japanese: 11時30分以降は歩行者は東側も利用できる」という簡単な選択を示しました。

slashRows.english: A bicycle symbol remained crossed out until 2:00.
slashRows.japanese: 自転車の印は午後2時まで禁止表示のままです。

slashRows.english: The board did not claim that one route was always best.
slashRows.japanese: 案内板は、どれか一つの道がいつでも最善だとは言いません。

slashRows.english: It connected the map, the time of arrival, and the transport schedule so visitors could make a safe choice for their own situation.
slashRows.japanese: 地図、到着時刻、交通時刻表を結び付け、それぞれの状況に合った安全な選択ができるようにしました。

passages.title: The Interview Quote with No Date
passages.body: The school newspaper was preparing an article about a new community sports park. A reporter found a strong quote in an old interview file: ‘We expect the park to open next spring.’ The sentence fit the article, so the first draft used it without a date. Before publication, Akira checked when the interview had been recorded. It was from eighteen months earlier. Since then, construction had been delayed twice, and the current city page listed a different opening season. The reporter did not delete the quote because it still showed what planners had expected at that time. Instead, the article identified the interview date and added the current schedule in the next sentence. The team also checked two other quotations whose timing might affect their meaning. Those dates were already clear. By adding one missing date, the newspaper avoided making an old expectation sound like a current promise. That context mattered.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校新聞は、新しい地域スポーツ公園についての記事を準備していました。記者は以前のインタビュー資料から、「来年の春に公園を開く予定です」という印象的な発言を見つけました。記事に合っていたため、最初の原稿では日付を示さずに使っていました。発行前にアキラが録音時期を確認すると、それは1年半前のものでした。その後、工事は二度遅れ、現在の市のページには別の開園時期が書かれていました。記者は、その発言が当時の計画を示していることには意味があるため、削除しませんでした。その代わり、インタビューの日付を示し、次の文に現在の予定を加えました。チームは、時期によって意味が変わる可能性のあるほかの二つの引用も確認しましたが、そちらの日付は明確でした。一つの欠けた日付を加えることで、昔の予想を現在の約束のように見せることを避けられました。その背景は重要でした。

passages.title: Two Counts of the Same Birds
passages.body: A nature club surveyed birds in a riverside park and found two very different results. On Tuesday morning, one team counted forty-two small birds. On Thursday evening, another team counted only twenty-six. At first, several students said the birds must leave the park later in the day. Mika was not sure. She compared the survey sheets and found three other differences. The morning team had walked the north path, where many berry bushes grew. The evening team had used the south path beside the sports field. Tuesday had been cool and cloudy, while Thursday had been warm and windy. The two teams had also counted for different lengths of time. To test the idea more fairly, the club repeated the survey twice the following week. Both teams used the same north path for thirty minutes. One survey began at 7:30 a.m. and the other at 5:30 p.m. The morning count was thirty-six and the evening count was thirty-two, a much smaller difference than before. The students could not conclude that time had no effect, but they also could not claim that it explained the first large gap. In their report, they listed time, weather, route, and counting area as factors that had changed. They included all four counts instead of choosing only the numbers that supported their first idea. The club learned that two measurements can look comparable while being taken under conditions that are not actually the same.
passages.fullTranslation: 自然観察部が川沿いの公園で鳥の調査をしたところ、二つの結果に大きな違いがありました。火曜日の朝、一つの班は小鳥を42羽数えました。木曜日の夕方、別の班は26羽しか数えませんでした。最初、何人かの生徒は、鳥は一日の遅い時間になると公園からいなくなるに違いないと言いました。しかしミカは確信できませんでした。調査用紙を比べると、ほかにも三つの違いがありました。朝の班は木の実のなる低木が多い北側の道を歩いていました。夕方の班は運動場のそばの南側の道を使っていました。火曜日は涼しく曇っていましたが、木曜日は暖かく風が強い日でした。また、二つの班は数えた時間の長さも違っていました。その考えをより公平に確かめるため、部は翌週に二度調査をやり直しました。今度は両方の班が同じ北側の道を30分間使いました。一方は午前7時30分、もう一方は午後5時30分に始めました。朝は36羽、夕方は32羽で、前回より差はかなり小さくなりました。時間がまったく影響しないとは言えませんが、最初の大きな差を時間だけで説明することもできません。報告書には、時刻、天候、道、観察範囲を変化した条件として書きました。最初の考えに合う数字だけを選ばず、四つの結果をすべて示しました。二つの測定値が比べられそうに見えても、実際には同じ条件で得られていないことがあると学びました。

slashRows.english: A nature club surveyed birds in a riverside park and found two very different results.
slashRows.japanese: 自然観察部が川沿いの公園で鳥の調査をしたところ、二つの結果に大きな違いがありました。

slashRows.english: On Tuesday morning, one team counted forty-two small birds.
slashRows.japanese: 火曜日の朝、一つの班は小鳥を42羽数えました。

slashRows.english: On Thursday evening, another team counted only twenty-six.
slashRows.japanese: 木曜日の夕方、別の班は26羽しか数えませんでした。

slashRows.english: At first, several students said the birds must leave the park later in the day.
slashRows.japanese: 最初、何人かの生徒は、鳥は一日の遅い時間になると公園からいなくなるに違いないと言いました。

slashRows.english: Mika was not sure.
slashRows.japanese: しかしミカは確信できませんでした。

slashRows.english: She compared the survey sheets and found three other differences.
slashRows.japanese: 調査用紙を比べると、ほかにも三つの違いがありました。

slashRows.english: The morning team had walked the north path, where many berry bushes grew.
slashRows.japanese: 朝の班は木の実のなる低木が多い北側の道を歩いていました。

slashRows.english: The evening team had used the south path beside the sports field.
slashRows.japanese: 夕方の班は運動場のそばの南側の道を使っていました。

slashRows.english: Tuesday had been cool and cloudy, while Thursday had been warm and windy.
slashRows.japanese: 火曜日は涼しく曇っていましたが、木曜日は暖かく風が強い日でした。

slashRows.english: The two teams had also counted for different lengths of time.
slashRows.japanese: また、二つの班は数えた時間の長さも違っていました。

slashRows.english: To test the idea more fairly, the club repeated the survey twice the following week.
slashRows.japanese: その考えをより公平に確かめるため、部は翌週に二度調査をやり直しました。

slashRows.english: Both teams used the same north path for thirty minutes.
slashRows.japanese: 今度は両方の班が同じ北側の道を30分間使いました。

slashRows.english: One survey began at 7:30 a.m. and the other at 5:30 p.m.
slashRows.japanese: 一方は午前7時30分、もう一方は午後5時30分に始めました。

slashRows.english: The morning count was thirty-six and the evening count was thirty-two, a much smaller difference than before.
slashRows.japanese: 朝は36羽、夕方は32羽で、前回より差はかなり小さくなりました。

slashRows.english: The students could not conclude that time had no effect, but they also could not claim that it explained the first large gap.
slashRows.japanese: 時間がまったく影響しないとは言えませんが、最初の大きな差を時間だけで説明することもできません。

slashRows.english: In their report, they listed time, weather, route, and counting area as factors that had changed.
slashRows.japanese: 報告書には、時刻、天候、道、観察範囲を変化した条件として書きました。

slashRows.english: They included all four counts instead of choosing only the numbers that supported their first idea.
slashRows.japanese: 最初の考えに合う数字だけを選ばず、四つの結果をすべて示しました。

slashRows.english: The club learned that two measurements can look comparable while being taken under conditions that are not actually the same.
slashRows.japanese: 二つの測定値が比べられそうに見えても、実際には同じ条件で得られていないことがあると学びました。

passages.title: The Museum Entry Plan
passages.material: capacity table + timed-entry card + floor guide
passages.body:
Class 3-2 was planning a museum visit for forty students and four adults. The museum required school groups to reserve entry times for three popular rooms. The class wanted to see all three before lunch, but the first plan did not fit the rules. Instead of guessing, the planning team put the capacity table, timed-entry card, and floor guide next to one another.

The capacity table listed Local Life Room: 24 people, Industry Room: 30 people, and Special Gallery: 20 people. The timed-entry card offered starting times at 10:00, 10:40, and 11:20. A group needed about thirty minutes in each room, and the museum allowed no more than two school groups to begin at the same time. The floor guide showed that Local Life and Industry were on the first floor. The Special Gallery was upstairs, and walking there from either first-floor room took about seven minutes. The class lunch reservation was at 12:20 in a hall beside the entrance. Everyone needed to be back there by 12:10.

The first draft divided the class into two groups of twenty-two. At 10:00, Group A would enter Local Life and Group B would enter Industry. At 10:40, both groups would exchange rooms. At 11:20, they would both enter the Special Gallery. That final step was impossible because forty-four people could not enter a room with capacity twenty.

The team considered making three groups, but the timed-entry rule created another problem. Three groups could not all start a reserved room at 10:00. So the students kept two groups but changed the order. Group A, twenty-two people, used Local Life at 10:00 and Industry at 10:40. Group B, also twenty-two, used Industry at 10:00, walked upstairs, and entered the Special Gallery at 10:40. At 11:20, Group A split temporarily: eighteen students and two adults entered the Special Gallery, while the remaining four students and two adults visited a free exhibit nearby. Group B used Local Life at 11:20. The small group from A could visit the free exhibit first and then join the others after the reserved room.

The revised plan was not perfectly equal, but it satisfied every capacity and starting-time rule. It also gave the class time to return downstairs and reach lunch by 12:10. The students wrote one note beside the plan: room order may differ, but every student will see the same three main exhibits. By linking the three materials, the team found a workable schedule without pretending that one simple route could fit all forty-four visitors.
passages.fullTranslation:
3年2組は、生徒40人と大人4人で博物館を見学する計画を立てていました。博物館では、人気のある三つの部屋について学校団体が入場時刻を予約する必要がありました。昼食前に三つすべてを見たいと考えましたが、最初の計画は規則に合っていませんでした。そこで推測せず、定員表、時間指定入場カード、館内図を並べて確認しました。

定員表には、くらしの部屋24人、産業の部屋30人、特別展示室20人とありました。時間指定入場は10時、10時40分、11時20分から選べます。一つの部屋の見学には約30分かかり、同じ開始時刻に入れる学校団体は二つまでです。館内図では、くらしの部屋と産業の部屋は1階にあります。特別展示室は上階にあり、どちらの1階の部屋からも歩いて約7分かかります。昼食は入口横のホールで12時20分に予約しており、全員が12時10分までに戻る必要があります。

最初の案では、クラスを22人ずつの二班に分けました。10時にA班がくらしの部屋、B班が産業の部屋へ入ります。10時40分に二班が部屋を交換し、11時20分には両方の班が特別展示室へ入る計画でした。しかし最後は不可能です。定員20人の部屋に44人は入れません。

三班に分ける案も考えましたが、今度は時間指定の規則が問題になりました。10時に三班すべてが予約部屋へ入ることはできません。そこで二班のまま、順序を変えました。22人のA班は10時にくらし、10時40分に産業を見ます。同じく22人のB班は10時に産業を見た後、上階へ移動して10時40分に特別展示室へ入ります。11時20分、A班は一時的に分かれ、生徒18人と大人2人が特別展示室へ入り、残りの生徒4人と大人2人は近くの自由見学展示を見ます。B班は11時20分にくらしの部屋へ入ります。A班の小グループは先に自由展示を見て、予約部屋の見学後に合流できます。

修正版は完全に同じ行程ではありませんが、すべての定員と開始時刻の規則を満たします。また、クラスには階下へ戻って12時10分までに昼食場所へ着く時間も残ります。生徒たちは計画の横に「部屋を見る順番は違っても、全員が同じ三つの主要展示を見る」と書きました。三つの資料を結び付けることで、44人全員が一つの単純な順路を通れるふりをせず、実行可能な予定を作ることができました。

passages.title: The Photo That Changed the Story
passages.body: The school newspaper received a photo from a sports day practice. The cropped image showed one runner far ahead while the others were standing near the starting line. A student wrote a caption saying that the runner had begun before everyone else during the race. Before publishing it, Hana asked for the original photo. The wider image showed a teacher holding a red flag and a board that said ‘Practice Start.’ The camera time also showed that the picture had been taken twenty minutes before the real race. The runner was testing the course alone while the other students waited for instructions. The newspaper changed the caption to explain that the photo showed a practice check, not an unfair start. It also added a rule for future photo work: when cropping changes who or what can be seen, reporters should check the original image before deciding what happened. The smaller picture had not been false, but it had removed information that changed the meaning of the scene.
passages.fullTranslation: 学校新聞は、体育祭の練習で撮られた写真を受け取りました。切り取られた写真には、一人の走者がずっと前にいて、ほかの生徒はスタート地点の近くに立っている様子が写っていました。ある生徒は、本番の競走でその走者がみんなより先に走り始めたという説明を書きました。掲載前にハナは元の写真を見せてもらいました。広い範囲が写った元画像には、赤い旗を持つ先生と「練習開始」と書かれたボードがありました。撮影時刻を確認すると、本番の競走より20分前でした。その走者は一人でコースを確認し、ほかの生徒は指示を待っていたのです。新聞は説明文を変え、不公平なスタートではなく練習確認の場面だと示しました。また、今後の写真利用について「切り取りによって見える人物や物が変わる場合、何が起きたか判断する前に元画像を確認する」という決まりを加えました。小さい写真そのものが偽物だったわけではありませんが、場面の意味を変える情報が取り除かれていました。

passages.title: Repair or Replace the Benches?
passages.body:
Three wooden benches in a neighborhood park needed attention. Some residents asked the city to replace all of them, while others wanted to repair everything to save money. A student group collected information before making a recommendation. Bench A had one damaged board, but its frame was strong. Repairing it would cost 8,000 yen and was expected to add about four years of use. Bench B had faded paint and two loose screws. A 4,000-yen repair could keep it useful for at least three more years. Bench C looked better from a distance, but the inspection found deep damage inside two legs. Repairing it would cost 22,000 yen and might add only one year. A new bench cost 30,000 yen.

The students also read user comments and observed the park on two afternoons. Bench A stood beside the playground and was used often by adults watching children. Bench B was near the walking path and was popular with older visitors. Bench C was behind a storage building and was used only twice during the observation. At first, the group thought replacing C in the same place would complete the project neatly. However, several visitors had asked for a seat near a large shade tree on the opposite side of the park.

The final proposal treated the three benches differently. A and B would be repaired because their structures were sound and people used them regularly. C would be removed because an expensive repair would not last long. Instead of replacing it in the same low-use location, the city could place one new bench near the shade tree. The students explained that ‘repair’ and ‘replace’ were not competing answers for the whole park. Cost, expected life, safety, location, and actual use had to be considered for each bench separately.

passages.title: The Heat-Safe Festival Schedule
passages.material: hourly forecast + site map + performance timetable
passages.body:
The city youth committee was helping with an outdoor festival scheduled for a hot Saturday. The first program placed all performances on one stage from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. After a heat-safety meeting, the students were asked to check whether the schedule still made sense. They used three materials: an hourly forecast, a site map, and the performance timetable.

The forecast showed 29°C at 10:00, 32°C at 11:00, 34°C at noon, 35°C at 1:00, and 33°C at 2:00. The site map marked the main stage in an open square, a smaller stage beside a row of trees, and a community hall with air conditioning. The hall could hold only 120 people, while the main stage area could hold more than 400. The timetable included a children's dance at 10:20, a school band at 11:30, a forty-minute local music show at 12:40, and a senior dance group at 2:00.

At first, the committee considered moving every event indoors after noon. That plan failed because the hall was too small for the local music show, which usually attracted more than 250 visitors. The students then compared the needs of each group. The children's dance would finish before the hottest hours. The school band could use the tree-side stage, where shade covered most of the waiting area by 11:30. The senior dance group needed a cooler place because several members had asked for shorter outdoor activity. The local music show had the largest audience and could not fit in the hall.

The revised schedule kept the children's dance at the main stage. It moved the school band to the shaded small stage at 11:30. The local music show remained on the main stage but moved from 12:40 to 2:10, when the forecast was beginning to fall. The senior dance moved indoors at 12:50. The committee also added free-water points and a twenty-minute open break around 1:30 so no group had to fill that period simply because the original schedule had used it.

The students did not claim that the new plan removed all heat risk. Weather could change, and real conditions still needed to be checked that morning. Their plan showed a different idea: use the forecast together with shade, room capacity, audience size, and the needs of performers. A schedule was safer when the materials were read as one set instead of one table at a time.
passages.fullTranslation:
市の青少年委員会は、暑い土曜日に予定されている屋外祭りの手伝いをしていました。最初のプログラムでは、午前10時から午後3時まで、すべての発表を一つのステージで行うことになっていました。暑さ対策の会議の後、生徒たちはその予定が今も適切かを確認するよう求められました。使った資料は、時間ごとの天気予報、会場地図、発表時刻表の三つです。

予報は、10時29度、11時32度、正午34度、午後1時35度、午後2時33度を示していました。地図には、開けた広場のメインステージ、木々の列のそばの小ステージ、冷房のある地域ホールが示されていました。ホールは120人までしか入れませんが、メインステージ周辺には400人以上入れます。時刻表には、10時20分の子どものダンス、11時30分の学校バンド、12時40分から40分間の地域音楽ステージ、午後2時の高齢者ダンスがありました。

最初、委員会は正午以降のすべての催しを屋内へ移すことを考えました。しかし、地域音楽ステージには通常250人以上が集まるため、ホールでは小さすぎました。そこで生徒たちは各グループの条件を比べました。子どものダンスは最も暑い時間より前に終わります。学校バンドは11時30分には待機場所の大部分が日陰になる木のそばのステージを使えます。高齢者ダンスでは、何人かが屋外活動を短くしたいと希望していたため、より涼しい場所が必要でした。地域音楽ステージは観客が最も多く、ホールには入りません。

修正版では、子どものダンスはメインステージのままにしました。学校バンドは11時30分に日陰の小ステージへ移しました。地域音楽ステージはメインステージのままですが、12時40分から、気温が下がり始める予報の午後2時10分へ移しました。高齢者ダンスは12時50分に屋内へ移しました。また、無料の給水場所を設け、午後1時30分ごろに20分間の空き時間を作りました。元の予定でその時間が埋まっていたからというだけで、無理に別の発表を入れないためです。

生徒たちは、新しい計画で暑さの危険がすべてなくなるとは言いませんでした。天気は変わる可能性があり、当日の朝に実際の状態を確認する必要があります。計画が示したのは別の考え方です。予報だけでなく、日陰、部屋の定員、観客数、出演者の必要を一緒に使います。一つずつ資料を見るのではなく、資料を一組として読む方が、より安全な予定を作れるのです。

After a heat-safety meeting, the students were asked to check whether the schedule still made sense.
They used three materials: an hourly forecast, a site map, and the performance timetable.
The forecast showed 29°C at 10:00, 32°C at 11:00, 34°C at noon, 35°C at 1:00, and 33°C at 2:00.
The site map marked the main stage in an open square, a smaller stage beside a row of trees, and a community hall with air conditioning.
The hall could hold only 120 people, while the main stage area could hold more than 400.
The timetable included a children's dance at 10:20, a school band at 11:30, a forty-minute local music show at 12:40, and a senior dance group at 2:00.
At first, the committee considered moving every event indoors after noon.
That plan failed because the hall was too small for the local music show, which usually attracted more than 250 visitors.
The students then compared the needs of each group.
The children's dance would finish before the hottest hours.
The school band could use the tree-side stage, where shade covered most of the waiting area by 11:30.
The senior dance group needed a cooler place because several members had asked for shorter outdoor activity.
The local music show had the largest audience and could not fit in the hall.
The revised schedule kept the children's dance at the main stage.
It moved the school band to the shaded small stage at 11:30.
The local music show remained on the main stage but moved from 12:40 to 2:10, when the forecast was beginning to fall.
The senior dance moved indoors at 12:50.
The committee also added free-water points and a twenty-minute open break around 1:30 so no group had to fill that period simply because the original schedule had used it.
The students did not claim that the new plan removed all heat risk.
Weather could change, and real conditions still needed to be checked that morning.
Their plan showed a different idea: use the forecast together with shade, room capacity, audience size, and the needs of performers.
A schedule was safer when the materials were read as one set instead of one table at a time.

最初のプログラムでは、午前10時から午後3時まで、すべての発表を一つのステージで行うことになっていました。
暑さ対策の会議の後、生徒たちはその予定が今も適切かを確認するよう求められました。
使った資料は、時間ごとの天気予報、会場地図、発表時刻表の三つです。
予報は、10時29度、11時32度、正午34度、午後1時35度、午後2時33度を示していました。
地図には、開けた広場のメインステージ、木々の列のそばの小ステージ、冷房のある地域ホールが示されていました。
ホールは120人までしか入れませんが、メインステージ周辺には400人以上入れます。
時刻表には、10時20分の子どものダンス、11時30分の学校バンド、12時40分から40分間の地域音楽ステージ、午後2時の高齢者ダンスがありました。

しかし、地域音楽ステージには通常250人以上が集まるため、ホールでは小さすぎました。
そこで生徒たちは各グループの条件を比べました。
子どものダンスは最も暑い時間より前に終わります。
学校バンドは11時30分には待機場所の大部分が日陰になる木のそばのステージを使えます。
高齢者ダンスでは、何人かが屋外活動を短くしたいと希望していたため、より涼しい場所が必要でした。
地域音楽ステージは観客が最も多く、ホールには入りません。

学校バンドは11時30分に日陰の小ステージへ移しました。
地域音楽ステージはメインステージのままですが、12時40分から、気温が下がり始める予報の午後2時10分へ移しました。
高齢者ダンスは12時50分に屋内へ移しました。

計画が示したのは別の考え方です。
予報だけでなく、日陰、部屋の定員、観客数、出演者の必要を一緒に使います。
一つずつ資料を見るのではなく、資料を一組として読む方が、より安全な予定を作れるのです。

passages.title: A Source behind the Famous Number
passages.body:
A number about the town appeared again and again in posters, speeches, and social media: ‘Eighty percent of local teenagers volunteer every month.’ A newspaper club wanted to use the number in an article about community service. Before printing it, Riku tried to find the original source. Several websites repeated the same sentence but did not explain where it came from.

He finally found a city report from two years earlier. The report did contain the number 80 percent, but the survey had been given only to members of school volunteer clubs. The question asked about joining at least one activity during the previous three months. It did not ask about volunteering every month. The famous sentence had changed both the group and the time period.

The club did not conclude that teenagers were uninterested in volunteering. The report could not answer that larger question. In the article, they wrote that 80 percent of surveyed volunteer-club members had participated at least once in three months. They also explained why this was different from saying 80 percent of all local teenagers volunteered monthly. Tracing the number to its source made the statement less dramatic but much more accurate.

ようやく2年前の市の報告書を見つけました。そこには確かに80％という数字がありましたが、調査対象は学校のボランティア部に所属する人だけでした。また質問は、過去3か月に少なくとも一度活動へ参加した経験についてのものでした。毎月ボランティアをしているかを尋ねたものではありませんでした。有名になった文は、対象となる集団と期間の両方を変えていたのです。

passages.title: The Shared Garden Water Plan
passages.body:
Residents of a community garden shared one water tank, but arguments increased during a dry summer. Some gardeners said every bed should receive the same amount of water. Others said the sunny beds needed more. A student science group offered to study the problem for two weeks.

The garden had twelve beds. Six were in full sun for most of the afternoon, and six were shaded by a building after 1:00 p.m. The students first checked the soil at the same depth each evening. They also read the watering log instead of relying on memory. During the first week, each bed received the same amount of water. By the third day, four sunny beds were dry before evening, while three shaded beds still had wet soil the next morning. The students did not immediately double the water for every sunny bed because plant type and soil were not identical.

For the second week, they created two starting schedules. Sunny beds received a smaller amount in the morning and another check in late afternoon. Shaded beds received one morning watering, followed by an extra amount only when the soil check showed it was needed. Gardeners recorded both the amount of water and whether the soil was dry, damp, or wet before watering. At the end of the week, fewer beds reached either extreme. The sunny beds did not stay dry for long periods, and the shaded beds were less often overwatered.

The students recommended keeping the two schedules as a guide, not as an automatic rule. A newly planted bed or a rainy day could require a different choice. They also suggested reviewing the log every Sunday so residents could see whether the pattern was changing with the season. Equal treatment, they explained, did not always mean equal amounts. A fair plan could use the same goal—healthy plants with less wasted water—while responding to different conditions.
passages.fullTranslation:
地域の共同菜園では一つの水タンクを共有していましたが、乾燥した夏に水やりをめぐる意見の対立が増えました。すべての区画に同じ量の水を与えるべきだという人もいれば、日当たりのよい区画にはもっと必要だという人もいました。生徒の科学グループが2週間調べることにしました。

菜園には12区画ありました。6区画は午後の大部分に日が当たり、残り6区画は午後1時以降、建物の影に入ります。生徒たちはまず、毎晩同じ深さで土の状態を確認しました。また、記憶だけに頼らず水やり記録も読みました。最初の週は、すべての区画に同じ量を与えました。3日目までに、日当たりのよい4区画は夕方前に乾いていましたが、日陰の3区画では翌朝も土が湿っていました。ただし植物の種類や土が完全に同じではないため、日なたのすべての区画の水をすぐ二倍にはしませんでした。

2週目には二つの基本予定を作りました。日なたの区画には朝に少なめに与え、夕方遅くにもう一度状態を確認します。日陰の区画は朝に一度水をやり、その後は土の確認で必要と分かった場合だけ追加します。利用者は、水の量だけでなく、水やり前の土が「乾いている・少し湿っている・湿っている」のどれかも記録しました。週の終わりには、極端に乾く区画も、極端に水が多い区画も減りました。日なたが長時間乾いたままになることが減り、日陰で水を与えすぎることも少なくなりました。

生徒たちは二つの予定を、自動的に従う規則ではなく目安として残すよう提案しました。植えたばかりの区画や雨の日なら、別の判断が必要になることがあります。また、季節とともに傾向が変わっていないか分かるよう、毎週日曜日に記録を見直すことも提案しました。同じように扱うことが、いつも同じ量を与えることを意味するわけではありません。健康な植物を育て、水の無駄を減らすという同じ目標を持ちながら、異なる条件に応じるのが公平な計画だと説明しました。

passages.title: When Two Witnesses Disagree
passages.body:
Two students saw a bicycle fall near the school gate, but their stories sounded different. One said, ‘The rider was going too fast and hit the curb.’ The other said, ‘A bag fell first, and then the bicycle turned.’ A safety committee wanted to describe the incident in a report without choosing a story simply because one sounded more confident.

The committee asked each witness to separate what was directly seen from what was assumed. passages.title: The Audio Guide Trial
passages.body:
A local history museum tested two versions of an audio guide. Version A gave a long explanation at the beginning of each room. Version B divided the same information into shorter tracks beside individual objects. The museum asked twelve students to try both versions on different floors. They recorded how many tracks each student finished and asked which facts they remembered afterward.

Most students said Version A sounded smooth, but several stopped listening before the long track ended. With Version B, more tracks were completed, although some students felt the story was less connected. The memory questions showed no clear winner: students remembered dates slightly better with B, while they explained the overall story better after A.

The student team did not recommend deleting either design. Instead, it suggested a short opening story for each room, followed by optional object tracks. Important dates could also appear on the screen. Their trial showed that ‘shorter’ and ‘better’ were not the same question. The best guide could combine continuity with choices for visitors who wanted more or less detail.

地域の歴史博物館は、音声ガイドの二つの版を試しました。A版は各部屋の最初に長い説明を流します。B版は同じ情報を短い音声に分け、個々の展示物のそばで聞けるようにしていました。博物館は12人の生徒に、別々の階で両方を試してもらいました。各生徒が何本の音声を最後まで聞いたかを記録し、その後どの事実を覚えているかも尋ねました。

多くの生徒はA版の話の流れが自然だと言いましたが、長い音声が終わる前に聞くのをやめた人もいました。B版では最後まで聞かれた音声が増えましたが、話全体のつながりが弱いと感じた生徒もいました。記憶を確かめる質問では、はっきりした勝者はありませんでした。日付はB版の方が少しよく覚えられていましたが、全体の話はA版の後の方がうまく説明できました。

生徒チームは、どちらか一方をなくすことを勧めませんでした。代わりに、各部屋の最初に短い全体説明を置き、その後に必要に応じて聞ける展示物ごとの音声を付ける案を出しました。重要な日付は画面にも表示できます。試験から分かったのは、「短いこと」と「良いこと」は同じ問いではないということでした。最も使いやすい案は、話のつながりを保ちながら、詳しく聞きたい人と短く聞きたい人の両方に選択肢を与えるものでした。

passages.title: The Evacuation Center Supply Choice
passages.material: supply list + room map + forecast table
passages.body:
After a strong typhoon warning, a town prepared to open an elementary school as an evacuation center. A junior-high volunteer team helped decide how to move emergency supplies from the town warehouse. The warehouse had enough goods for several days, but the school had limited storage space. The students received three materials: a supply list, a room map, and a forecast table.

The supply list showed 240 bottles of water, 120 ready-to-eat meals, 80 blankets, 60 folding mats, 12 battery lamps, and 10 large boxes of hygiene goods. The town expected about 70 people at first, including ten children and eight older residents. The room map showed that the gym could hold people but had almost no locked storage. A classroom near the entrance had secure cabinets but only twelve square meters of free floor space. A small nurse's room had power outlets and could keep medicine-related equipment away from crowded areas. The forecast table predicted the strongest wind from 9:00 p.m. until 2:00 a.m., with rain continuing through the next morning. A second delivery from the warehouse could not be promised during that period.

The first suggestion was simple: take one half of every supply to the school. The students noticed two problems. Half of the folding mats would not be enough if most evacuees needed a dry place to rest, while half of the hygiene boxes would use valuable storage even though not all of them were needed immediately. The team also had to leave safe walking space in the gym.

They made a priority plan. All sixty mats and all eighty blankets would go first because the storm could prevent another trip during the night. One hundred forty bottles of water and ninety meals would cover the expected group with extra supplies for late arrivals. Six lamps would be placed in different rooms, with the remaining lamps kept at the warehouse for other shelters. Four hygiene boxes would go into the locked classroom cabinets, and medicine-related equipment would be placed in the nurse's room near power outlets. The remaining water, meals, and hygiene goods would stay ready for a later delivery if roads were safe.

The team wrote the reasons beside each number. The plan was not based on which items looked equally divided. It considered expected people, night-time risk, storage space, room function, and the possibility that transport would stop. They also marked the quantities as a first plan, not a fixed answer. If more evacuees arrived before 9:00 p.m., the numbers would have to be checked again.
passages.fullTranslation:
強い台風の警報を受け、町は小学校を避難所として開く準備をしました。中学生のボランティアチームは、町の倉庫から非常用品をどのように運ぶか考える手伝いをしました。倉庫には数日分の物資がありましたが、学校の保管場所には限りがあります。生徒たちは、物資一覧、部屋の地図、天気予報表の三つの資料を受け取りました。

物資一覧には、水240本、すぐ食べられる食事120食、毛布80枚、折り畳みマット60枚、電池式ランプ12個、衛生用品の大箱10個がありました。町は最初、子ども10人と高齢者8人を含む約70人が来ると見込んでいました。地図によると、体育館には人を収容できますが、鍵のかかる保管場所はほとんどありません。入口近くの教室には安全な収納棚がありますが、空いている床は12平方メートルだけです。小さな保健室にはコンセントがあり、薬に関係する機器を混雑する場所から離して置けます。予報では、最も強い風は午後9時から午前2時までで、雨は翌朝まで続く見込みでした。その間に倉庫から二度目の配送ができる保証はありません。

最初の案は単純で、すべての物資を半分ずつ学校へ運ぶというものでした。しかし生徒たちは二つの問題に気付きました。避難者の多くが乾いた場所で休む必要があるなら、折り畳みマットの半分では足りません。一方、衛生用品の箱を半分運ぶと、すぐにはすべて必要でないのに大切な保管場所を多く使います。また、体育館には安全に歩ける空間も残す必要があります。

そこで優先順位を付けました。夜間に嵐で追加の輸送ができなくなる可能性があるため、マット60枚と毛布80枚はすべて先に運びます。水140本と食事90食なら、予想人数に加えて遅れて来る人の分も用意できます。ランプは6個を各部屋に分け、残りは別の避難所のため倉庫に残します。衛生用品は4箱を鍵付きの教室棚へ入れ、薬に関係する機器はコンセントのある保健室に置きます。残りの水、食事、衛生用品は、道路が安全なら後から運べるよう倉庫で待機させます。

チームはそれぞれの数量の横に理由を書きました。計画は、すべてを同じ割合に分けることを基準にしたのではありません。予想される人数、夜の危険、保管場所、部屋の役割、交通が止まる可能性を一緒に考えました。また、数量は固定した答えではなく最初の計画だと明記しました。午後9時より前に予想以上の避難者が来れば、もう一度数量を確認する必要があります。

englishSentences: After a strong typhoon warning, a town prepared to open an elementary school as an evacuation center.
A junior-high volunteer team helped decide how to move emergency supplies from the town warehouse.
The warehouse had enough goods for several days, but the school had limited storage space.
The students received three materials: a supply list, a room map, and a forecast table.
The supply list showed 240 bottles of water, 120 ready-to-eat meals, 80 blankets, 60 folding mats, 12 battery lamps, and 10 large boxes of hygiene goods.
The town expected about 70 people at first, including ten children and eight older residents.
The room map showed that the gym could hold people but had almost no locked storage.
A classroom near the entrance had secure cabinets but only twelve square meters of free floor space.
A small nurse's room had power outlets and could keep medicine-related equipment away from crowded areas.
The forecast table predicted the strongest wind from 9:00 p.m. until 2:00 a.m., with rain continuing through the next morning.
A second delivery from the warehouse could not be promised during that period.
The first suggestion was simple: take one half of every supply to the school.
The students noticed two problems.

Half of the folding mats would not be enough if most evacuees needed a dry place to rest, while half of the hygiene boxes would use valuable storage even though not all of them were needed immediately.
The team also had to leave safe walking space in the gym.
They made a priority plan.
All sixty mats and all eighty blankets would go first because the storm could prevent another trip during the night.
One hundred forty bottles of water and ninety meals would cover the expected group with extra supplies for late arrivals.
Six lamps would be placed in different rooms, with the remaining lamps kept at the warehouse for other shelters.
Four hygiene boxes would go into the locked classroom cabinets, and medicine-related equipment would be placed in the nurse's room near power outlets.
The remaining water, meals, and hygiene goods would stay ready for a later delivery if roads were safe.
The team wrote the reasons beside each number.
The plan was not based on which items looked equally divided.
It considered expected people, night-time risk, storage space, room function, and the possibility that transport would stop.
They also marked the quantities as a first plan, not a fixed answer.
If more evacuees arrived before 9:00 p.m., the numbers would have to be checked again.
japaneseSentences: 強い台風の警報を受け、町は小学校を避難所として開く準備をしました。
中学生のボランティアチームは、町の倉庫から非常用品をどのように運ぶか考える手伝いをしました。
倉庫には数日分の物資がありましたが、学校の保管場所には限りがあります。
生徒たちは、物資一覧、部屋の地図、天気予報表の三つの資料を受け取りました。
物資一覧には、水240本、すぐ食べられる食事120食、毛布80枚、折り畳みマット60枚、電池式ランプ12個、衛生用品の大箱10個がありました。
町は最初、子ども10人と高齢者8人を含む約70人が来ると見込んでいました。
地図によると、体育館には人を収容できますが、鍵のかかる保管場所はほとんどありません。
入口近くの教室には安全な収納棚がありますが、空いている床は12平方メートルだけです。
小さな保健室にはコンセントがあり、薬に関係する機器を混雑する場所から離して置けます。
予報では、最も強い風は午後9時から午前2時までで、雨は翌朝まで続く見込みでした。
その間に倉庫から二度目の配送ができる保証はありません。
最初の案は単純で、すべての物資を半分ずつ学校へ運ぶというものでした。
しかし生徒たちは二つの問題に気付きました。
避難者の多くが乾いた場所で休む必要があるなら、折り畳みマットの半分では足りません。
一方、衛生用品の箱を半分運ぶと、すぐにはすべて必要でないのに大切な保管場所を多く使います。
また、体育館には安全に歩ける空間も残す必要があります。
そこで優先順位を付けました。
夜間に嵐で追加の輸送ができなくなる可能性があるため、マット60枚と毛布80枚はすべて先に運びます。
水140本と食事90食なら、予想人数に加えて遅れて来る人の分も用意できます。
ランプは6個を各部屋に分け、残りは別の避難所のため倉庫に残します。
衛生用品は4箱を鍵付きの教室棚へ入れ、薬に関係する機器はコンセントのある保健室に置きます。
残りの水、食事、衛生用品は、道路が安全なら後から運べるよう倉庫で待機させます。
チームはそれぞれの数量の横に理由を書きました。
計画は、すべてを同じ割合に分けることを基準にしたのではありません。
予想される人数、夜の危険、保管場所、部屋の役割、交通が止まる可能性を一緒に考えました。
また、数量は固定した答えではなく最初の計画だと明記しました。
午後9時より前に予想以上の避難者が来れば、もう一度数量を確認する必要があります。

passages.title: The Headline before the Evidence
passages.body:
The school news site prepared a headline after a student survey: ‘Students Want Longer Lunch Breaks.’ The survey did show that 62 percent chose a longer lunch period, so the headline seemed reasonable. Before publication, Emi read the response sheet more closely. Only thirty-two students had answered, and twenty-four of them were members of clubs that practiced during lunch.

The survey had been shared through a club leaders' message group, not with the whole school. That did not make the answers useless, but it changed what the results could show. The editors replaced the headline with ‘Many Club Survey Respondents Prefer a Longer Lunch Break.’ In the article, they explained how the survey had been distributed and listed the number of responses.

They also planned a second survey using several homerooms before making a statement about all students. The first headline was shorter and stronger, but it went beyond the evidence. The revised version made the sample visible to readers and left room for a better question later.
passages.fullTranslation:
学校のニュースサイトは、生徒アンケートをもとに「生徒は昼休みを長くしたがっている」という見出しを準備しました。調査では確かに62％が長い昼休みを選んでいたので、その見出しはもっともらしく見えました。公開前にエミが回答表を詳しく見ると、回答したのは32人だけで、そのうち24人は昼休みに練習する部活動のメンバーでした。

アンケートは学校全体ではなく、部長たちの連絡グループを通して配られていました。だから回答に意味がないわけではありませんが、結果から言える範囲は変わります。編集者たちは見出しを「部活動向け調査の回答者の多くが、長い昼休みを希望」に変えました。記事には、アンケートをどのように配ったかと回答数も書きました。

また、全校生徒について述べる前に、いくつかの学級を使って二度目の調査を行うことにしました。最初の見出しは短く力強いものでしたが、証拠から言える範囲を超えていました。修正版では読者に調査対象が見えるようになり、後でより良い問いを調べる余地も残しました。

passages.title: The Tree Record from Two Years
passages.body:
A class project compared the growth of street trees using a city record from two years earlier. The old table listed trunk size, tree height, and location. Students measured the same streets again and were excited when several trees appeared to have grown very quickly.

Before writing their report, Kenta checked the identification numbers. Three numbers from the old table were missing, and three new numbers appeared in the current list. A city worker explained that damaged trees had been removed after a storm and new trees had been planted nearby. One new tree stood only two meters from an old location, so comparing those two rows would falsely look like unusual growth.

The class separated trees with matching identification numbers from replacements. It calculated growth only for the trees that could be followed across both years. The report still mentioned the removed and newly planted trees, but in a different section. By checking identity before comparing measurements, the students avoided treating two different trees as one continuous record.
passages.fullTranslation:
あるクラスの活動では、2年前の市の記録を使って街路樹の成長を比べました。古い表には幹の太さ、木の高さ、場所が載っていました。生徒たちは同じ通りをもう一度測り、いくつかの木がとても速く成長したように見えたので驚きました。

報告を書く前に、ケンタが識別番号を確認しました。古い表の番号が三つなくなり、現在の一覧には新しい番号が三つ増えていました。市の担当者によると、嵐の後に傷んだ木を撤去し、その近くへ新しい木を植えたとのことでした。新しい木の一つは古い場所から2メートルしか離れていなかったため、その二つの行を比べると、実際には別の木なのに異常に大きく成長したように見えてしまいます。

クラスは、同じ識別番号を持つ木と植え替えられた木を分けました。成長量は、2年間を通して同じ木だと確認できるものだけで計算しました。撤去された木と新しく植えた木についても報告には書きましたが、別の項目にしました。測定値を比べる前に木の同一性を確認したことで、異なる二本の木を一つの連続した記録として扱う誤りを避けられました。
